correctness.rationale: From 2025 component and Chow theorems plus 2026 SNC/Hilbert-polynomial theorem, integer projection degrees form a permutation matrix; each component is a coordinate line. A cycle would force a forbidden triple point, so the graph is a forest, while chi(O)=1 forces h−1 edges, hence a tree. Tree normalization and explicit extension of ambient sections prove H1=0, h0=1+sum d and restriction surjectivity for every nonnegative multidegree. The relative Hilbert series and K-polynomial follow formally. Cartwright–Sturmfels Proposition 4.4 and Theorem 4.1 then place the scheme in the closure of the diagonal orbit. No finite computation is used as infinite proof.

value.rationale: The 2026 paper explicitly poses the embedded-flatness and complete-Hilbert-series questions. Their complete rank-one case is a natural boundary: it identifies the linked-net curves with the classical diagonal Hilbert scheme and shows no rank-one obstruction to embedded smoothing, while distinguishing embedded smoothing from net smoothability. The exact all-degree coordinate ring answers a finer question than the published Hilbert polynomial, albeit via a short bridge to strong classical results.
